subject: Film & Cinema
title: CGI: The Digital Revolution
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: CGI: The Digital Revolution.

hook.text: Jurassic Park's dinosaurs looked real in 1993. They still hold up. Most modern CGI doesn't.

buildup.text: CGI lets filmmakers create anything imaginable — worlds, creatures, physics-defying action.

discovery.text: The best CGI is invisible — set extensions, crowd duplication, and sky replacements you never notice.

twist.text: Overreliance on CGI produces 'weightless' action that audiences increasingly find unconvincing.

climax.text: CGI is a tool, not a style. Used with restraint, it's magic. Used without it, it's a cartoon.

punchline.text: The best effect is the one you never see.

quiz.question: What made Jurassic Park's CGI so enduring?
options: Combining limited, careful CGI with practical animatronic dinosaurs
